This is the voice of the higher realm, and it concerns a matter of the utmost importance. The matter is this: to warn mankind, to rouse them and awaken them, to protect them in this world from evil and corruption, and to protect them in the Hereafter from the Fire. It is also to show them the way to salvation and the wisdom of success in the test before time runs out. The truth is that this is a very great responsibility, especially when it is placed upon a single human being. Even if that human being is a Prophet and Messenger, because man is so astray, rebellious, defiant, disobedient, obstinate, crooked, and insistent upon his own way, that reforming any human being is a very difficult task. Compared even with the most difficult tasks of the world, this is more difficult still.

﴿O you who are wrapped up in garments, arise and warn!﴾ (74:1-2). Among the duties of prophethood, the greatest duty is that people be warned of an evil end, and be alerted that the danger is very near. The punishment lies in ambush for those who are heedless and who rush headlong along evil paths, and who have no awareness or sense of the danger. This shows how greatly Allah sympathises with His servants and how merciful He is. Despite the fact that if all of mankind went astray, they could not diminish the kingdom of Allah by even an atom's weight, and if all of them were guided, they could not add anything to the kingdom of Allah, it is still Allah's mercy and grace that He makes such extensive arrangements to save them from the painful punishment of the Hereafter. In this world He protects people from evil, and He sends Messengers saying: come, I will forgive you and, by My grace and bounty, admit you into Paradise.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verse 3:

After entrusting the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) with this great duty, specific instructions are now given concerning his own person.

(1) The first instruction: proclaim the greatness of your Lord.

﴿And your Lord, glorify [Allahu Akbar]﴾ (74:3). That is, proclaim the greatness of Allah alone, because in reality, greatness belongs to Allah alone, and He alone deserves to have the takbir (the cry of "Allahu Akbar") raised for Him. This instruction shows that in the Islamic worldview, within the concept of ilah (deity) and tawhid (the oneness of Allah), it is included that Allah alone is great.

Every individual, every thing, every value, and every reality is small and insignificant in comparison with Allah, while Allah alone is the Great and the Most High. Before the majestic greatness of Allah, all celestial bodies, all bulk, all powers, all values, all events, all circumstances, all meanings, and all forms vanish and become non-existent, while Allah becomes ever more Great, Exalted and Higher.

The Prophet (ﷺ) is instructed that, armed with this lofty concept and the weapons of this exalted creed, he should take upon himself the duty of warning and alerting the world, and of confronting circumstances and difficulties, and bearing their hardships and burdens. Therefore, against this concept, all the plots of the opponents will be false, all their powers will be worthless, and all obstacles will be removed. If the caller (da'i) holds the true conception that the Lord whose call he has taken up is the greatest, then no difficulty can stand before him. The hardships and trials of the Islamic call demand that the greatness of Allah and the belief in His supremacy remain present in the mind of the human being.

(2) The second directive is given:

﴿And your garments, keep them pure﴾ (74:4). This is a metaphor for purity of heart, of character, and of conduct. It refers to the purity of the personality, which includes outward cleanliness and also all those matters that are connected in some way with the person of the Prophet. It is through spiritual and moral purity alone that a person can derive intimations from the higher realm. Purity is inherent in the nature of prophethood, and therefore purity is commanded here. Then, for the duty of prophethood, for conveying the message to people, for warning them, and for the work of the Islamic call amid different kinds of people, different kinds of desires, and different ups and downs, it was necessary that his skirt be free of every stain and blemish. Moreover, after the duty of prophethood was entrusted to him, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had to go among every kind of people, among whom were base people and filthy people, those who were immersed in filth and pollution. His instruction was that he was to carry out the task of the Islamic call without becoming involved in these filths and pollutions. This is a most important and profound indication for all those who take up the work of the Islamic call and who stand in the position of the heirs of the prophets, and who must work while living among every kind of people. They must work in every kind of circumstance and in every kind of society and community.

(3) You are instructed to abandon shirk and all those deeds that would be a cause of punishment in the Hereafter.

"And keep away from uncleanness" (74:5). The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was already abstaining from every kind of shirk and from those things that would cause punishment in the Hereafter. Even before being invested with the office of prophethood, he was acting upon this guidance, for in accordance with the demand of his sound nature (fitrah salimah), he had abandoned these evils before receiving the command from Allah. He was distant from every ideological, moral, customary and practical jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance). There is no report in which it is mentioned that he took part in any pagan custom or idolatrous act. Therefore, this instruction is in essence a declaration that you should keep away from these things, and that these things do not accord with Islam. No Islamic way of life can be combined with them. Hence, you have been instructed, by way of emphasis, to keep away from these things.

"Rijz" (ر‌جز) means punishment; afterwards its application was extended to those things that are causes of punishment, meaning: do not even go near these things.

(4) This guidance is also given to you: keep your personal interests away from the work of prophethood, and do not display a favour over the great work you are carrying out.

﴿And do not give, seeking to receive more.﴾ (74:6) The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was to expend a great deal in the life of da'wah; he was to spend all his material, moral and physical strength on this path and to make sacrifices. Yet what the Lord required of him was that he should not regard this great struggle as great, and should not display a favour upon anyone. If a person in the path of Islamic da'wah develops the feeling that he has done a great deal, he can never remain a da'i (caller to Islam). The struggle in this path takes on the colour of greatness only when it is forgotten, and rather when the awareness settles firmly within the human self that whatever is being expended on this path is given by Allah alone. It is Allah who chose us for this purpose, granted us success and resources, and made us worthy of it. This is simply Allah's grace, His choosing, His honouring, and the esteem He bestowed upon us by enabling us to undertake this work. Our duty is to give thanks to Allah for this religion of His, not to display a favour over anyone.

(5) At the end, the Prophet ﷺ is given the instruction that whatever befalls him, he should be patient.

﴿And for the sake of your Lord, be patient﴾ (74:7). In the Qur'an, Allah repeatedly enjoins patience upon those engaged in the call to Islam (da'wah), and in truth patience is the real equipment in the path of da'wah. It is a battle fought on three fronts: on one side, a struggle against one's own desires and inclinations; on the other, a struggle against the enemies of the call to Islam. These enemies are in the grip of satans and fight for their interests and desires. Then there is the long struggle, the scarcity of resources, and the reward, which is entirely in the Hereafter; no worldly benefit is attached to this effort. One must also struggle against these circumstances, purely for the pleasure of Allah.

Once these important instructions were given to the Prophet ﷺ, it is now explained what it is that he is to warn the people of. This matter is brought forward in a nutshell: that terrifying Day is presented before them, the Day with which you are to warn the people.

Fa-idha ........................ al-naqur (74:8) — The word al-naqur also means the horn that is blown, but the root naqr carries the sense of a harsh, striking sound, and this harshness is intended to point to the harshness of that Day. It is as though the naqur is struck and a severe sound comes out of it, and this sound falls on the ears like a blow. Therefore that Day will be very severe for the disbelievers, and there will be no ease for them in it.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verse 10:

"...upon the disbelievers, it will not be easy" (74:10). This entire day will be harsh, so harsh that there will be no ease in it. Therefore, understand that on that day there will be extreme distress and severe constriction, and so be cautious about it. Make your preparations before the Trumpet (ṣūr) is sounded. In this way, the scene of that day is presented before them.

Now the address turns to a specific denier, an obstinate opponent who rejects the truth. It becomes apparent that this person was a particular antagonist of the Islamic call, and he would employ every stratagem against the call. Accordingly, he is given a severe warning, and his portrait is drawn in such a way that those who hear it know well who he is. All the features of this person have been given in this written image, and this personality appears clearly in plain words. Let us now observe:

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verses 11–14:

Many narrations state that these verses refer to Walid ibn Mughirah al-Makhzumi. Allamah Ibn Jarir narrates from Ibn Abd al-A'la, who narrates from Muhammad ibn Thawr, who narrates from Ma'mar, who narrates from Ubadah ibn Mansur, who narrates from Ikrimah, that Walid ibn Mughirah came to the Prophet (ﷺ). The Prophet (ﷺ) recited the Holy Qur'an before him. His heart softened. This reached Abu Jahl ibn Hisham. He came to him and said, "Your people want to collect wealth for you." He said, "For what?" He said, "They want to give you this wealth because you went to Muhammad and he has had an effect on you." (Abu Jahl sought to make use of his sense of self-respect; he knew that this was a man of pride.) Walid said, "The Quraysh know that I am the wealthiest man among them." Abu Jahl said, "Then say something about him, so that people understand that you dislike his words and deny Muhammad's teachings." Walid said, "What should I say about him? By God, none of you is as skilled as Muhammad in literature and poetry. I know all the kinds of poetry: rajaz, qasidah, and I know verses of every kind. His speech does not resemble any of them, but there is a sweetness in his speech; whatever comes before it is crushed, and whoever wishes to rise above it, it rises above him." Abu Jahl said, "By God, your people will never be pleased with you until you say something about him." He said, "Let me think." When he thought, he said, "This speech is a magic that has been transmitted from earlier times." Upon this, these verses were revealed:

From "Dharni" ........ "Wahid" (74:11) ... to "Alayha tis'ata 'ashar" (74:30).

In another narration, it is stated that after Walid's meeting with the Prophet (ﷺ), the Quraysh said that if Walid became irreligious, the entire tribe of Quraysh would become irreligious. Abu Jahl said that he would set Walid right. After this, Abu Jahl came to Walid, and after lengthy reflection he said, "This is ancient magic. Do you not see that it separates a man from his household? It separates the father from the son and creates division between the master and the slave."

This is the incident as it appears in the narrations. But the Qur'an presents it in extremely vivid and luminous words, with a highly effective style. It begins thus:

"Dharni ... wahida" (74:11): "Leave me with the one whom I created alone." This address is to the Prophet (ﷺ). The meaning is that the person whom I created alone, when he had none of those things in which the people of the world take pride, namely wealth, property, children and other things such as honour and respect in society, I gave these to him, and now he behaves arrogantly over them, wages war against the Islamic movement, and plots conspiracies. Leave him to me; I shall deal with him. At this point, when a person reflects a little, he trembles and thinks that against this wretch the boundless power and might of the All-Knowing, All-Aware has set to work. It is the might of Allah, the Compeller, the Subduer. This power will grind that insignificant and weak one to dust, and what will his condition be then.

This verse describes the features of this man at some length and also gives the details of the blessings of Allah that He bestowed upon him. These details are given before the mention of his aversion and his plots: that I created him alone, he had nothing, not even clothes on his body. After that, Allah gave him vast wealth, and gave him many sons who were always present around him, and because of them he was regarded as extremely honourable. And Allah provided him with every means of livelihood for his life and made every difficulty easy for him.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verse 15:

﴿Then he aspires that I should give him more.﴾ (74:15) That is, he is not content with the wealth he already has. He wants more, yet he neither shows contentment nor offers thanks. Or he aspires that revelation should also descend upon him and that he be given a Book, as is mentioned at the end of the surah.

﴿Nay, every one of them desires that he be given open scrolls.﴾ (74:52) This man was among those who envied Muhammad (ﷺ), asking why he had become a prophet.

This is where he is rebuked and faces severe reproach.

"Indahu kana li-ayatina 'anida" (74:12): "Indeed, he was hostile to Our verses." Out of obstinacy he rejected the proofs of the truth and did not accept the signs that lead to faith. He stood against the Islamic call, began a war against the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), prevented people from Islam, and spread misleading propaganda against it.

After this most severe rebuke, he is now threatened, and as a result the comforts he enjoyed turn into hardships, and ease gives way to difficulties.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verse 17:

﴿Sa-arhaquhu sa'ouda﴾ (74:17) "I will make him climb a steep ascent." This is the best possible image and depiction of hardship and difficulty. Climbing a steep ascent is an extremely laborious act, and it becomes hard for a person to draw breath. And if this task is forced upon someone and the climber has no personal interest in it, the act becomes even more difficult. This image and depiction is also a true expression of the reality. For the one who turns away from the straight, smooth and pleasant path of faith will face difficulties on the path of deviation. Countless roughnesses and hardships arise, and the life of such a person passes in anguish and restlessness. He always remains bewildered and distressed, as though he were being made to climb a great height and being raised upon a gallows. In his life there is neither freshness, nor comfort, nor joy, nor tranquility, nor even the hope that, through the fatigue of this journey, he will reach his destination.

Now there is drawn the crude picture of this person's mental state and inner psychology, in which every person contradicts his own impressions and feelings. He puts pressure on his nerves, a frown appears on his forehead, and he makes a grimace. And he applies all his mental and intellectual energy to the purpose of finding some fault within the Qur'an and the Bearer of the Qur'an.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verse 18:

"Indeed, he thought and planned. So may he be destroyed, how he planned! Again, may he be destroyed, how he planned! Then he looked around. Then he frowned and scowled. Then he turned away and became arrogant. At last he said: 'This is nothing but magic transmitted from before; this is nothing but the speech of a human being.'" (74:18-25)

The manner of expression is such that every moment, every thought and every movement is being depicted. It is as if the pen of a skilled painter is drawing a picture, not merely words but colours being filled in. Or rather, it is as if a film is running, and each scene is coming before the eyes, changing moment by moment.

In one picture, one sees that the man is immersed in deep thought and contemplation. In this scene he is also given a curse.

Then, ﴿فَقُتِلَ﴾ "May he be killed!" This is a severe mockery.

﴿كَيْفَ قَدَّرَ﴾ "How he contrived!" It means: see what kind of statement he tried to devise. After this, the curse is repeated.

Then, woe to him! How he calculated! (74:20)

In the next picture he looks around, makes a face, knits his brow, and adopts a ridiculous expression, one full of extreme artificiality.

All this contrivance and thinking yields him no reasonable result. So he is compelled to call the bright day night and to call the truth falsehood.

All this contrivance and thinking yields him no reasonable result. So he is compelled to call the bright day night and to call the truth falsehood.

This is a commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 74, verse 25:

"This is nothing but magic learned from others; this is nothing but the word of a human being."

These are living moments that the Noble Qur'an gives the form of words. They convey an imagery so powerful and clear that it is more vivid than a painting, and more striking and enchanting than a moving pen. The person who has been depicted is given, until the Day of Resurrection, a portrait of ridicule, hatefulness and utter ugliness, which people of generations have seen and read, and will continue to see and read. After this portrayal, a terrifying threat is now addressed to this person.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verses 26–28:

﴿Soa-saqar﴾ (74:26): "And what will make you know what Saqar is?" It is a terrifying thing, beyond the reach of our power of comprehension. After this general description and this admission of our lack of knowledge, certain severe characteristics of Hell are mentioned.

﴿La tubqi wa la tadhar﴾ (74:27): "It leaves nothing, and spares nothing." It is something that sweeps everything away and annihilates everything. No thing can stand before it, nor does anything remain from it, nor is anything left over from it; it reduces everything to nothing.

Now, what is its treatment of the human being?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verse 29:

﴿لَوَّاحَةٌ لِّلْبَشَرِ﴾ (74:29) "Scorching the skin." As was said in Surah al-Ma'arij:

﴿تَدْعُو مَنْ أَدْبَرَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ﴾ (70:17) "It calls to everyone who turns his back and walks away." It calls all of them to itself, and its scene is extremely frightening... Then, standing over it are its guards and overseers:

﴿Over it are ... nineteen﴾ (74:30). These are the angels appointed to oversee it. They are extremely powerful. Alternatively, it may be some other creation with the qualities of angels, or a category of angels. Whatever the case, Allah has told us that they are nineteen, and we believe in this.

As for the believers, since they held firm conviction in the Being of the Lord, they affirmed it upon hearing the Word of Allah, and they adopted the attitude that a servant should adopt towards his Lord. Therefore they had no doubt. As for the polytheists, they made this number of angels a source of trial, because their hearts were empty of faith. Their hearts did not hold the proper reverence for the Being of the Lord, and they were not serious about this grave matter. So, upon hearing it, they began to mock and ridicule, and treating it as a strange thing, they started to joke about it. Some said, "Can ten of you not confront one of these nineteen?" Others said, "Just confront two of them, and leave the rest to me; I will take care of them." With this blind, narrow-minded and obstinate spirit, they received this great Book.

The following verses were revealed about this matter. In them is an explanation of why knowledge of a point from the hidden treasures of Allah's unseen was disclosed, why the number nineteen was fixed, and this matter is referred back to the knowledge of the unseen of Allah. It is also explained what is intended and purposed by the mention of Hell, its angels, and the number of its workers.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verse 31:

The verse begins by stating that these angels are nineteen, and the polytheists doubt this number.

Wa ma ja'alna ... malaikah (74:31) "We have made the keepers of Hell none but angels." These keepers are among those angels who possess extraordinary power, and only Allah knows their nature and disposition. They are extremely strong, and about them Allah has said:

La ya'soonallaha ma amarahum wa yaf'aloona ma yu'marun (74:31) "They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do whatever they are commanded." That is, they follow the commands of Allah, and they have the strength to carry out whatever Allah orders. Allah has granted them such power that they carry out His command immediately. If Allah has commanded them to carry out His orders within the fire, then He has given them the capacity to function in such conditions, just as He taught them. So how can these wretched creatures ever contend with these angels? Those who said that they would overpower these angels spoke out of ignorance. In truth, they have no knowledge of the power of Allah or the strength of Allah's hosts, and they do not know how Allah manages His affairs.

Wa ma ja'alna ... kafaru (74:31) "And We have made their number a trial for the disbelievers." These disbelievers in fact express astonishment at the number of these angels. They do not know which matters cannot be settled without submission, and which matters leave room for dispute and debate. This is a matter of the unseen, and in it there is no alternative to submission and acceptance. For man possesses neither little nor much knowledge of these unseen realms and subjects. When Allah has informed us through His Prophet, and the Prophet is truthful and Allah is truthful, then there is no room for argument and debate. The proper station of a human being is simply to accept the word of the Prophet and to be assured that what Allah has told is sufficient, and that there is good in confining oneself to it, and that there is no room for debate on it. Disputation can only be undertaken on a subject about which one has some prior knowledge and objects to new knowledge. Regarding the number of the angels, man has no prior knowledge at all, and as for their being nineteen, the knowledge of this belongs to Allah alone: what they are and why they are nineteen. Anyone who objects may object even to the number twenty. Why were the heavens made seven? This too could be questioned. Why was man created in his present form, from dry clay, and why were the jinn created from a flame of fire? Why does a human remain nine months in the mother's womb, and why do tortoises live for thousands of years? And why this, and why that? The only answer is that it is the will of Allah, and this is the true answer to such matters.

Li yastaiqina ... wal-mu'minun (74:31) "So that the People of the Book may be certain and the believers may increase in faith, and that the People of the Book and the believers may not be in doubt." Both of these groups will find material for certainty in the number of the keepers of Hell, and the faith of the believers will increase. As for the People of the Book, they certainly have some knowledge on this matter, and when they hear that the Holy Qur'an also confirms this, they will accept it as correct, because the Holy Qur'an is a confirmer of previous scriptures. As for the believers, their faith increases with every new verse, because their hearts are open and they are constantly connected through the Messenger to the higher realm. Whatever truths come to them become a cause of increase in their faith. In time, the wisdom behind why Allah appointed nineteen angels will settle in their hearts, for there is always some wisdom in the system of Allah's creation and governance. When this truth settles in the minds of both groups, neither will doubt, because this matter has been revealed from Allah.

Wa liyaqula ... mathalan (74:31) "And those in whose hearts is a disease and the disbelievers will say, 'What does Allah mean by this strange statement?'" Thus the effect of this same truth differs among hearts. Those given the Book believe, the believers grow in faith, while those with disease in their hearts, the weak in faith and the hypocrites, ask in bewilderment and wonder:

Ma dha arada Allahu bihadha mathalan (74:31) "What does Allah mean by this example?" Because they do not understand the wisdom of this number, and they do not in principle accept that there is some wisdom in all the affairs of the Creator of the universe. They neither offer confirmation of the reports of Allah and His Messenger ﷺ, nor do they believe that in every act of Allah there is hidden goodness and wisdom.

Kadhalika yudillu Allahu man yasha'u wa yahdi man yasha'u (74:31) "Thus Allah leads astray whom He wills and guides whom He wills." "Thus" means: through the exposition of these truths and through the exposition of the verses of the Qur'an, Allah affects different hearts in different ways. One group takes guidance from them according to the will of Allah, while another group is led astray under the system of His will. For the ultimate cause of every matter is the absolute will of Allah. Divine power has given human beings both kinds of capacity: within them is the capacity for guidance and also the capacity for misguidance, and this capacity lies within the system of Allah's will. So whoever is misguided is also within His will, and whoever is guided is likewise within that domain, because both kinds of capacity have been placed within their creation. Both paths have been made easy for them, and whoever takes whichever path, he is within the sphere of Allah's will, and this sphere is founded upon Allah's profound wisdom.

The concept that Allah's will is absolute and unrestricted, and that whatever occurs in this universe occurs within the sphere of that will, is a broad concept, and it is wider than the narrow debates of the theologians (mutakallimun) about human compulsion and free choice. It is a discussion that can never reach a decisive conclusion, because debates about compulsion and choice are conducted from a very narrow angle.

These debates are conducted within the limited thinking and limited reasoning of man, and within the limited conceptions of man, whereas the system of Allah's will is connected with the system of His unlimited divinity.

Allah has shown mankind the path of guidance and error, and has also shown the method by which, by following it, we may attain felicity and success, and the ways through which people go astray and reach a bad end. After this, Allah has not obligated us to know more than this, nor has He given us power and capacity beyond this. Allah's word is that My will is unrestricted, and whatever I wish comes to pass. Therefore we should understand the unrestricted will and absolute decree of Allah according to our understanding and perception, and act accordingly. We should walk the path that leads to guidance and avoid the path by which we go astray, and we should not engage in vain and fruitless debate on matters which the faculties of human perception cannot reach. In accordance with this principle, the debates of the theologians on the subject of qadar and free choice are fruitless.

We cannot reach the reality of what Allah's will does concerning us. However, we can grasp the reality of how human beings become deserving of Allah's grace and mercy. Therefore we should devote our strength to those tasks for which we have been made responsible, and leave the hidden and ambiguous affairs of Allah to Allah. When Allah's will becomes manifest, we come to know that this was Allah's will and it has come to pass. Before the manifestation of His will, we cannot truly comprehend it. Behind every will there is a hidden wisdom, and this wisdom too is known to Allah alone. This is the method of a true believer.

Wa ma ya'lamu junuda rabbika illa huwa (74:31) "And none knows the hosts of your Lord except Him." Therefore the hosts of Allah, their reality, their functions and their power, are not known to us, because they are among the unseen matters of Allah. It is Allah's will to reveal any of these matters if He so wishes. And what Allah declares is decisive and binding. After Allah's word, no one can dispute it, no one is permitted to speak against it, nor to seek to know beyond it, for no one can actually do so.

Wa ma hiya illa dhikra lil-bashar (74:31) "And this is none other than a reminder for mankind." The pronoun in "hiya" refers either to the "hosts" of Allah or to Hell, and also to the angels who are upon it. These too are among the hosts of Allah, and their mention has been made to warn and admonish people, not merely for the sake of dispute and debate. Only the believers benefit from the words of Allah; as for misguided hearts, they turn these very things into a means of mere argument and contention.

After clarifying this unseen reality and explaining the ways and causes of guidance and misguidance, the discourse now connects the realities of the Hereafter, the reality of Hell, and the hidden powers of the Lord with the visible signs and evidences of this universe. People witness these visible signs yet display heedlessness and negligence, while they grope blindly in search of unseen realities. Yet through these visible matters and signs, the will and powers of Allah are clearly manifested, and through these outward signs it becomes evident that behind them lies a great purpose and a powerful will.

The moon and its phases, and the scenes of night as it ends and the morning dawns, are tremendous sights and displays. They are eye-opening scenes, and they have countless effects upon the human heart and mind. If a person reflects upon them, many secrets are unveiled to him, and they have countless effects upon the human heart and mind. And if a person reflects upon them, many secrets are unveiled to him. Many profound ideas come to the screen of a person's thought, and he attains firm awareness. The Qur'an, by drawing a person's attention to these phenomena, settles these ideas in his heart, and it knows these feelings well.

When the moon rises, moves through the expanse of the cosmos, and then disappears, if a person reflects upon it, it certainly places some secret of this universe into a person's ear. Sometimes, standing in the light of the moon and reflecting, a person is affected as though he has bathed in light.

The scene of the departing of the night is also wondrous: at the time of the dawn's appearance and in those tranquil moments before the sun rises, if a person looks with a seeing eye, he sees that a conscious will and the hand of power have removed one state and advanced another. In this scene, just as the world gradually becomes illumined, the seeing heart also becomes illumined. In short, only a seeing eye is needed, and awareness and perception.

Allah, the Creator of the human heart and sight, knows that these scenes leave deep effects upon human feelings. And sometimes these effects are so profound that a person thinks he has been created anew and is seeing it for the first time.

Behind these influences, illuminations and impressions, and behind the sun and moon, the night and day, and the appearance of morning, there is also another great reality, to which the Qur'an is drawing a person's attention. It is preparing the human heart and sight to perceive this reality: that in these phenomena are the signs of Allah's creative power, Allah's wise governance, and the tremendous order and arrangement of this universe, and that this universe moves with such a precise and intricate order that human intellect is astonished upon seeing it.

With these great cosmic realities, Allah swears an oath, awakening people drowned in heedlessness: try to understand the great values of Allah, and take a lesson from the signs and indications within them. That Hell, the divine angels stationed over it, the Hereafter, and its horrors are in fact among those great matters that are both wondrous and frightening, and these events are extremely perilous. Take them seriously.

It is as though the circumstances are dangerous, fear hangs over the atmosphere, and a state of emergency has broken out.

It is responsible for its deeds and its earnings. Every person will have what is due to him and will bear the burden of his own sins.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verse 42:

﴿What brought you into Saqar?﴾ ... And this scene has a deep effect on the hearts of the believers, who in this world were enduring severe torments at the hands of those criminals. Today they find themselves in a most exalted station in the Hereafter, while those who used to afflict them are in that humiliating position. This scene is so vivid and impactful that both parties find themselves present on the Day of Resurrection, as though the page of this world has been folded up and we are present on the plain of Resurrection.

And now, just read that lengthy confession of guilt which these deniers and arrogant ones made in the presence of Allah and the believers, and made with the utmost disgrace and humiliation.

They will say, "We were not among those who used to pray."

This indicates that we did not, by believing, join the group of those who prayed. From this it becomes clear how great the importance of prayer (salah) is in Islam. It is, as it were, a proof of faith and success, and denial of prayer is in fact disbelief (kufr), and the one who does not pray is deprived of the quality of faith.

"And we did not feed the poor." This is the second attribute. Prayer is among the attributes of servitude to God, and it relates to the Divine Being, whereas feeding the needy is an act of worship that relates to human beings themselves. The Qur'an has made the provision of sustenance for people a part of faith and has repeatedly emphasized it. In Arab society, where people would squander everything for the sake of pride and boasting, the poor and needy were dying of hunger and there was no one to ask after them. The Qur'an draws attention to this issue on a purely human basis, and it declares the feeding of the needy to be an act of worship done solely for the pleasure of God.

"And we used to engage in vain talk along with those who engaged in vain talk" (74:45) — here it is explained how boldly those people treated the Islamic worldview and Islamic belief, and how they regarded Islamic faith as mere idle chatter. For them, faith was a subject of ridicule and mockery. Yet faith and belief are an extremely serious matter with grave, dangerous and frightening consequences. It was a matter on which they ought to have reached a decision only after deep reflection and consideration. A decision on this was necessary before all other affairs of life, for the whole of life's direction depends on determining its conception, its awareness, its worth and its reality. Therefore, not deciding on this subject with seriousness and reflection was a foolish step, and we committed this folly by regarding such an important matter as mere idle talk.

"And we used to deny the Day of Judgment." This is the true root of that calamity: for the one who denies the Resurrection, all the values and measures of his life become disordered, and all his standards are thrown into turmoil. In his sensibilities, the horizon of life becomes very narrow and confined. His whole thinking is limited to the brief span of this earth, and he can think only about those outcomes that take place within this short life. Therefore he is never content with these outcomes, and no reckoning or accounting of the Hereafter lies before his mind. This is why all his criteria and all his assessments become corrupt. Corruption arises even in his worldly affairs, and all his undertakings end in evil.

The guilty say this, and they confess that our condition was such that we did not pray, did not feed the needy, remained engrossed in idle chatter and frivolous talk, and denied the Day of Judgment.

"Until there came to us the certainty." That is, we were struck by death, which ends all doubts and suspicions and settles the matter. This decision is so certain that no one can reject it. Now neither remorse is of any benefit, nor is repentance accepted, nor is there any time left for righteous deeds. Now the reality of the situation is certain to come about.

Here a comment is made on that wrong stance: now all hopes have been cut off, and these people have reached this end.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verse 48:

"Then the intercession of intercessors will not benefit them." Now the decision has been made and the word has been fulfilled. Everything has been decided, and this decision and this end is the true end of the guilty. Now no intercession will benefit these criminals, and even if we suppose that some intercession were to take place, it would still not avail them.

Having shown this humiliating and hopeless state of affairs, these people are once again called to attention: the opportunities that have been provided for them in this world, they should make use of them. But they turn away from this guidance and also prevent others from it; rather, they flee from goodness and guidance. And they flee from the means that are the true means of life, eternal life. Thus, a mocking glimpse is shown of the situation in which they are immersed.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verses 49–51:

﴿فَمَا لَهُمْ عَنِ التَّذْكِرَةِ مُعْرِضِينَ﴾ ... ﴿قَسْوَرَةٍ﴾

Wild donkeys are very timid creatures; when they hear the roar of a lion, they flee in whatever direction they are facing. The Arabs were familiar with such scenes. When human beings are likened to those frightened donkeys, the image becomes extremely ridiculous. The meaning is that their aversion and flight from reminder and admonition is not because they are facing any fear, but because a reminder is calling them to their Lord, and is providing them the opportunity to be saved from that dreadful end. In fact, this is a marvellous depiction by the Divine Hand, which recorded this comparison so that people would keep reading it until the Day of Resurrection, that such conduct would appear hateful, that people would keep avoiding such behaviour, and that those who adopted this attitude would keep hiding their faces in shame.

This was the external picture of these people: that they are wild donkeys who have fled from a lion. But what is their inner psychological state, and what is their conscious disquiet?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verse 52:

Bal yureedu ... munashsharah

This awareness [of their own position] was held by them out of envy toward the Prophet ﷺ, asking why this rank had been bestowed upon the Messenger ﷺ. Every one of them wished that this rank would be given to him, and that open scriptures would be seen descending upon each person. This is an allusion to the great men of Quraysh who seethed with jealousy over the fact that this Speech had been revealed upon Muhammad (ﷺ), the son of Abdullah.

Lau la ... 'azeem: "Why was this Qur'an not revealed upon some great man of the two cities?" But Allah said that He knows who is fit for the office of Messengership and whom He chooses for this great task. This was the very reason why these people disliked the Islamic outlook on life and were not ready to accept it.

The inner portrait of these people's souls continues. Therefore, another cause, filled with this greed, covetousness and envy, is also placed before us: why these people fell into this unjustified envy and covetousness. The more far-reaching cause is that these people do not believe in the Hereafter. For this reason they have been deprived of this grace and generosity of Allah.

﴿Nay! ... the Hereafter﴾

Their fearlessness and carelessness are what keep them away from this admonition and wisdom, and they are running away from the Islamic call. If the awareness of the Hereafter were present in their hearts, their condition would not be that they are caught up in doubt about every matter.

After this, they are warned once more. Now the final word is spoken, and they are left to do as they wish and to accept whatever outcome they choose.

Surah al-Muddaththir, verses 54–55 (Commentary of Sayyid Qutb, Fi Zilal al-Quran)

No, indeed, this is a reminder (kallā innahu tadhkirah). Whoever wishes may take heed of it.

This Qur'an, from which these people turn away and flee as wild donkeys flee, while their hearts are filled with envy and greed, and who are heedless of the Hereafter. It is only a reminder (tadhkirah), a warning (tabsirah) and an admonition (nasihah). Whoever wishes may take admonition from it, and whoever does not wish need not do so. Benefit and loss belong to each person himself. Whoever wishes may gain honour and Paradise, and whoever wishes may gain disgrace and Hell.

Having stated that people are free and independent in choosing good and evil, this reality is also brought forward: that their freedom and choice lie within the sphere of the Divine Will (mashi'ah ilahiyyah), and the Will of Allah is unrestricted. And ultimately all affairs are within the sphere of Allah's authority. This is the reality that the Qur'an clarifies on every occasion and in every context, so that a human being does not think that the Will of Allah is limited. The meaning is that human choice too lies within the sphere of the Will, and all events occur by the command and Will of Allah.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 74, verse 56:

ومایذکرون .................... المغفرة

Everything that occurs in this universe is bound within the greater system of Allah's will (mashiyyah). Events take place in accordance with the direction of Allah's will and within its vast scope. Therefore, no human act can occur without Allah's will. The divine will encompasses, within its own sphere, all the values of the earth, because all values are created by Allah's will, and human beings and the laws of nature (nawamis-i-fitrat) are created by Allah. The events that unfold in this universe move only along the track of the divine will, which has no limit or boundary. Within this track, every human being is both free and bound.

Reminder and admonition (tadhkir aur nasihat-amozi) occur only in accordance with Allah's grant of success (tawfiq). Allah knows who is deserving of it. Hearts lie between two of Allah's fingers; He turns them as He wills. If Allah knows that a person has a good intention, He turns him towards goodness.

But a human being has no knowledge of what Allah wills. Allah's will lies behind the veil of the unseen. However, he does know what Allah's pleasure is, and where it lies, and Allah has explained in the Qur'an where His pleasure lies. When a person advances on the path of Allah's pleasure, Allah grants him the success to advance further.

But the thing that Allah wishes to firmly establish in the consciousness of a believer is that Allah's will is unconditioned, and that Allah's will encompasses him, so that the entire attention of a sincere servant remains focused upon the Being of Allah, and a Muslim remains fully submitted before Allah. This is the fundamental truth without grasping which Islam cannot take root in a human heart. When this condition becomes firmly settled in the mind, and the human heart and vision are filled with it, and a person begins to interpret all the events and incidents of life in accordance with this conception, then he becomes a true Muslim. This is the purpose of the unconditioned nature of Allah's will, and this application of Allah's will is brought along with every decision in the Qur'an, whether it be the decision of Paradise and Hell, or the decision of a person's guidance or misguidance.

As for the historical and theological debate that arose about human compulsion and free choice (jabr and ikhtiyar), it does not reveal the whole reality. It merely takes one part of the total reality, and because of this, human thought has never arrived at a satisfying conclusion. This debate went off the correct and simple paths of the Qur'an onto extremely complicated paths, and the further this debate advanced, the narrower became the avenues for the free movement of human thought.

وما یذکرون ................ اللہ (74:56): "And they will not take heed, unless Allah wills it." Because they cannot oppose the system of Allah's will, and in no respect do they make any hostile movement. The movement and will of man also occur only within the wider sphere of the divine will.

ھواھل التقوی (74:56): "He is worthy that He be feared." Allah deserves that His servants fear Him, and therefore the demand upon them is that they fear Allah.

واھل المغفرة (74:56): "And He is worthy to forgive." He is capable of forgiving such people.

This grace He bestows upon whomever He wills, and Allah's grace occurs in accordance with His system of will. Taqwa alone makes a person worthy of forgiveness, and Allah deserves to be feared.

ھواھل ........................ المغفرة (74:56): "He is worthy that He be feared, and He is worthy to forgive those who fear Him."
